newsitem.title: USA: US lawmakers welcome FOMC decision - up to a point.
newsitem.headline: US lawmakers welcome FOMC decision - up to a point.

text.p: U.S. lawmakers on Wednesday welcomed the Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates unchanged -- up to a point.

Democratic Senator Tom Harkin, a long-time Fed critic, said the decision not to raise rates should come as a relief to the economy. But the Iowa lawmaker voiced disappointment that the central bank had not chosen to lower rates.

"With inflation well under control, and broad measures of economic activity, construction spending and factory orders declining, there are more reasons to lower interest rates rather than raising or holding rates steady," he said.
Rep. Jim Saxton, Chairman of the Congressional Joint Economic Committee, said the Fed's decision seemed appropriate given that there is little evidence of a pick-up in inflation.
However, the New Jersey Republican chastised the central bank for not being more open and explaining the reason why it had opted to leave interest rates unchanged.

"The public does deserve more information about policy decisions than a mere signal that no change has taken place," Saxton said. "Explaining why no action was taken is just as important as providing rationale for a change in policy. Such information helps markets work better."
